title: microexperiment safeguard bounded ops scratchpad (wip)
content:
Summary:
This is a working scratchpad for a light-weight microexperiment and bounded-ops guardrail approach to rollouts for LLM features (chat-safety, reranking model swap, token-batching tweak). The idea: run very small, short-lived microcohorts with strong, automated cutoffs and low blast radius, then scale via an explicit gated ramp. This doc collects proposed rules, fast abort heuristics, operator scripts, and questions for cross-functional review.

Objectives:
- Give product + SRE + ML a shared, low-friction canary pattern for small LLM changes (quantization profile, prompt template tweak, model variant).
- Keep blast radius negligible (<= 0.5% of traffic for first 1h) and ensure human-free auto-abort for obvious safety/cost regression.
- Enable quick experiments (1–2 hours) to detect gross regressions without heavy instrumentation work.

When to use this pattern:
- Non-blocking UX experiments where user-visible regression is reversible and not PII-sensitive.
- Model variant swaps for inference-cost/latency tuning where we want production signals before larger rollout.
- Config changes that affect cost per token or batching behavior.

High-level flow (operator-friendly):
1) Create microcohort (traffic slice) via Console -> create experiment -> micro-slice tag. Default size: 0.2% traffic, geo-balanced.
2) Launch for a short warm-up: 10 minutes baseline, then 50 minutes observation (total 1h).
3) Automated monitors evaluate safety/latency/cost metrics every minute; threshold breaches trigger instant full reversion.
4) If metrics clear, escalate to expanded cohort (1% for 2h) with additional checks.
5) Manual review and sign-off before >10% exposure.

Core automated cutoffs (auto-abort triggers):
- Safety regression: new toxicity/hallucination signal rate > baseline + 3 sigma AND absolute rate > 0.8% for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Latency: p95 latency increases > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows.
- Cost: average tokens-per-response increases > 40% leading to expected e2e cost delta > $0.002 per request (configurable).
- Error rate: 5xx or model errors > baseline + 0.5% for 3 minutes.
- Unknown template: sudden uptick in out-of-range structured outputs (schema failures) > 0.2%.

Signal design notes (pragmatic):
- We need cheap proxies for hallucination: 1) short regex checks for hallucination classes for targeted prompts, 2) lightweight semantic-similarity baseline checks using embeddings for critical tokens. These are stopgaps until full eval harness is wired.
- Use existing cost estimator pipeline to compute real-time estimated per-request cost from token profiles and runtime flags. Avoid slow offline cost jobs for microexperiments.

Operational checklist before launch (quick):
- [ ] Attach experiment to an existing alerting channel (pager/team slack) and set page-to on-call for the first hour.
- [ ] Confirm rollback playbook link attached to experiment metadata.
- [ ] Define who does manual triage if auto-abort fires (owner + on-call).
- [ ] Verify that model fallback variant exists and is tested (automated fallback must be healthy).
- [ ] Note expected token delta and baseline metrics in experiment description.

Sample canary config (defaults to copy into Console template):
- name: micro-batch-quant-profile-1
- exposure: 0.2% (geo-balanced, exclude EU beta users)
- duration: 1h (10m warmup + 50m observation)
- metrics: safety_hypo_rate, p95_latency_ms, error_rate, avg_tokens, est_cost_delta
- auto_abort_rules: as above
- rollback_action: immediate route to previous model variant + notify on-call

Escalation and comms:
- If auto-abort: immediate rollback + post-mortem stub created automatically in experiment workspace. Owner gets slack DM + email.
- If no auto-abort but janky signal (e.g., marginal safety increase with low volume): pause traffic, spin to 1% and extend test, contact ML owner for logs.
- For positive signals: capture a short blameless summary, snapshot eval prompts, and propose next step (1% -> 5% -> 25%).

Lightweight observability (must-haves for microexperiments):
- 1-min resolution metric streams for: safety proxy, latency p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, avg tokens, request volume.
- Mini-diffs: show relative delta vs baseline with confidence band estimate for the interval.
- Event log: annotated timeline (deploy time, abort events, manual pauses).

Operator scripts (quick commands) — rough pseudo: 
- Start: console create --template micro --variant v2 --exposure 0.2 --tags "micro-experiment"
- Monitor: rollout watch --exp micro-batch-quant-profile-1 --poll 60s --alerts slack:#prod-experiments
- Force abort: rollout abort --exp micro-batch-quant-profile-1 --reason "auto-abort safety breach"
- Promote: rollout promote --exp micro-batch-quant-profile-1 --to 1% --duration 2h

Known limitations / tradeoffs:
- Small sample sizes make fine-grained quality metrics noisy; we accept that microexperiments are for detecting large regressions, not subtle quality deltas.
- Proxy safety signals are imperfect; avoid microexperiments for high-risk features (fiat payments, PII transformations).
- Latency/cost signals sensitive to traffic mix; ensure cohort is balanced by region and user agent where possible.

Open questions to resolve in cross-functional review:
- What is the canonical safety proxy for short experiments? (embedding delta vs rule-based vs human-in-loop sampling).
- Should auto-abort thresholds be absolute or relative by class of feature? (example: chat vs reranker)
- Who gets paged on a weekend microexperiment? (current default: SRE on-call)
- How to wire the experiment to cost quotas to prevent billing surprises?

Next steps / actionable items:
- [Ravi] prototype 1-min safety proxy using existing embeddings infra (JIRA-PRJ-3421). Target: prototype by 2025-01-24.
- [Amelia] add Console template and prefilled experiment description. Target: 2025-01-18 (in progress).
- [Sofia] draft auto-abort unit test harness and simulate sample runs with rollout-simulator PR #128. Target: 2025-01-22.
- [Product] schedule 30m sync with SRE + ML + DS to finalize thresholds. Suggested by 2025-01-21.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally minimal — we want something practitioners will actually use without long config overhead. Think of it as "safety seatbelt" for tiny experiments.
- If you think the default exposure (0.2%) is too small for your metric sensitivity, note the use-case in comments; we can create per-team overrides.

Quick links / references:
- Fallback runbook (doc id): CONFLUENCE-4852
- Experiment simulator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-simulator/pull/128
- Related ticket (instrumentation): JIRA-PRJ-3421

Random jotting:
- Might be useful to have a single-button "micro-experiment with safety net" in Console that auto-populates checks.
- Consider auto-sampling 50 recent prompts for conditional human review if safety proxy crosses 1 sigma but not 3 sigma.

End of scratchpad (WIP).
